messages.author: 5baa09ab3ebac9af
messages.subject: Reducing CV
parts:
Hello List,

I am running Distance for a multi-species songbird project (point-transect) in three different locations. When I do my an overall density estimate (all three sites), my CV is not high, the intervals are e.g. 19-55.  I have tried truncating at two different distances >75 >100 meters.I post-stratified by site, and the CV went up (two sites had 50% CV and one 110% CV). The confidence intervals in spite of the models I use, are still huge.

How can I achieve lower CV and have smaller confidence intervals?

Sorry for this basic question. Any insights would be appreciated.

Thanks,

Carolina

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Reducing CV
parts:
Carolina:

It is not easy to answer your question for information you have provided.  Recognise that uncertainty in your estimates is a function both of uncertainty in the detection function (which is usually large in point transect sampling) as well as variability in encounter rate between points.  Perhaps when producing site-specific density estimates the variability in encounters between points is relatively large.  Without more information, it is not possible to say more.

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Reducing CV
parts:
Good afternoon list,

After I emailed, I exchanged different emails with Eric Rexstad, thanks once again Eric. Here a summary of what he recommended, in case this could be of insight for some of you:

The patterns I first reported resulted from analysis done with all species pooled. Recognizing that all species have different detection functions, my results  were influenced by this.

Bottom-line: If you have more than one study area, focus on species and site-specific differences rather than trying to make sense of the overall pooled data.

Sincerely,

Carolina



You could simply note that the patterns you had first reported had been for all species and all sites pooled.  That upon further analysis the patterns in the analysis became more clear.

messages.author: ee7030efbc184b5b
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Reducing CV
parts:
If transect sampling is performed  at one site for one species annually is increasing the number of samples the best way to reduce the CV for each year's density estimate?

Current CV% for annual density estimates range from 12 to 35% with density estimated using no defined intervals and a global detection function (across all years). Currently 3-5 samples are taken per year. For some years sampling was performed over the period of a month or more which gives me a little heartburn due to the differences in animal movement/behavior over that time as well as being able to compare estimates directly year to year but that's another issue.

Thanks for your help, Sarah
